Issued at 250 PM EDT Sun Oct 4 2026

Through Tonight...Isolated shower and storm activity developing 
across east central Florida is forecast to increase in coverage 
over the next several hours, with the highest coverage anticipated
near and north of the I-4 corridor (40-60%). Adequate daytime 
heating through this morning has helped increase instability 
across east central Florida and some drier air closer to the 
surface will assist in increasing downdraft potential this 
afternoon. Overall, lightning strikes and wind gusts up to 50 mph 
will be possible with storm activity this afternoon. A moist air 
mass remains in place across east central Florida, with the GOES19
Total PWAT viewer showing PWATs of 2-2.3". This moisture coupled 
with some slightly weaker steering flow will increase the risk of 
minor flooding, with quick rainfall accumulations of 1-3" 
possible. WPC has expanded the Marginal Risk (1/4) of excessive 
rainfall to include northern portions of east central Florida, 
primarily from Orlando to the Cape northward. While there is lower
confidence in activity along the coast, some southwesterly flow 
aloft may push activity towards the east coast late this afternoon
into the evening hours. Showers and storms are then anticipated 
to diminish, with mostly dry conditions forecast through the 
remainder of tonight. Some isolated development across the local 
Atlantic waters cannot be ruled out.

Afternoon temperatures remain on track to peak in the upper 80s 
to low 90s, with peak heat indices of 100F and greater already 
occurring in some spots across the area. Tonight, warm and muggy 
conditions persist with lows remaining above normal in the mid 
70s.

Monday-Tuesday...Broad mid-level troughing creeps southward 
across the southeastern US early this week, with shortwaves of 
energy traversing the trough. At the surface, a frontal boundary 
drifts southward, approaching north Florida on Monday and stalling
across the central Florida peninsula on Tuesday. An area of low 
pressure is anticipated to develop along the boundary near the 
Florida Panhandle on Monday, slowly drifting eastward across the 
state on Tuesday. Overall, this set-up will maintain a deep plume 
of moisture across east central Florida, with PWATs forecast to 
exceed 2" areawide, with some guidance indicating values could 
climb as high as 2.5" in some spots. This moist atmospheric 
profile coupled with warmer temperatures aloft will limit 
instability and reduce the amount of downdraft energy available, 
with lower confidence in seeing strong storm development on either
day. Some occasional lightning strikes cannot be fully ruled out 
at times in addition to an isolated gust up to 45 mph here and 
there. While storm activity will be limited, the flooding 
potential increases due to saturated soils and the potential for 
multiple rounds of showers. WPC has included all of east central 
Florida in a Marginal Risk (1/4) of excessive rainfall on Tuesday.
Flooding of low-lying and urban areas will be possible, and 
flooded roadways cannot be fully ruled out. Activity is 
anticipated to continue into the overnight hours each day, with 
the best chances for overnight activity forecast on Tuesday night 
as the low pressure moves across the peninsula. 

Increasing cloud coverage will help limit daytime heating across 
the peninsula, which will impact temperatures. Highs on Monday 
remain warm in the mid 80s to low 90s, trending downward into 
Tuesday with temperatures generally ranging from the low to mid 
80s from Orlando to the Cape northward and in the mid to upper 80s
southward. Humid conditions on Monday means there is a chance for
some spots to reach peak indices of 100F and greater, with lower 
confidence in this occurring on Tuesday. Lows remain near to 
slightly above normal in the upper 60s to mid 70s.

Wednesday-Saturday...The wet pattern will continue across east 
central Florida through the remainder of this week as the stalled 
frontal boundary remains draped across central Florida. Guidance 
remains split on the evolution of the aforementioned surface low 
riding along the boundary, though a brief period of it lingering 
off the east coast of Florida on Wednesday looks possible. This 
would have implications on beach, coastal, and marine conditions. 
Beyond Wednesday, the Euro and GFS diverge on solutions, with the 
GFS showing a strengthening low while the Euro trends it weaker. A
clearer picture on the evolution of the low is expected as 
guidance comes into better agreement with time. Regardless of the 
low, as mentioned, conditions remain wet across the area with 
above normal rain chances persisting (50-90%). With the moist air 
mass in place, confidence in storm development remains on the 
lower side through the remainder of the week. Flooding concerns
